question: Which of the following laws states that 'Every object will remain at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Newton's First Law of Motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion** states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force. This is also known as the **Law of Inertia**.
 
• This law implies that objects have a natural tendency to maintain their current state of motion unless influenced by an unbalanced force.
 
• The principle is fundamental to understanding the concept of inertia, which is the resistance of an object to change its state of motion or rest.
 
• For example, a book lying on a table will remain stationary unless a force, like a push, is applied to it, or a moving car will continue in motion unless brakes or friction are applied to stop it.
 
• This law is the foundation for analyzing motion and forces in classical mechanics, making it essential in physics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Law of Conservation of Momentum:**

 
 
• This law states that the total momentum of a closed system of objects (with no external forces acting) remains constant over time.
 
• It is mathematically expressed as: **m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ = constant**, where m and v represent mass and velocity of objects, respectively.
 
• This principle is critical in collision and explosion analyses.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Third Law of Motion:**
 
 
• This law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
• It explains phenomena like the recoil of a gun when fired or the propulsion of a rocket.
 
• Example: If you push against a wall, the wall pushes back with an equal and opposite force.
 
 
 
• **Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion:**
 
 
• These laws describe the motion of planets around the Sun.
 
• They include:
 
 
• The Law of Ellipses (planets move in elliptical orbits).
 
• The Law of Equal Areas (a line joining a planet and the Sun sweeps out equal areas during equal intervals of time).
 
• The Harmonic Law (the square of the orbital period of a planet is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit).
 
 
 
 
 
• **Inertia:**
 
 
• Inertia is the property of an object to resist changes in its state of motion or rest.
 
• It depends on the object's mass; higher mass means greater inertia.
 
• Example: A heavy truck requires more force to accelerate or decelerate compared to a small car.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Background:**

 
 
• Newton's First Law builds on Galileo's concept of inertia, which was formulated during his experiments with inclined planes.
 
• Galileo proposed that in the absence of friction, a moving object would continue moving indefinitely.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Understanding why seat belts are necessary in cars to protect passengers during sudden stops or collisions.
 
• Explains why objects in space continue moving without any propulsion due to the lack of external forces like friction.
 
 
 
• **Practical Observations:**
 
 
• When a bus suddenly stops, passengers tend to lurch forward due to inertia.
 
• Objects on a conveyor belt in factories remain stationary until external forces act upon them.
